59480428.t: Al Qaranah Archaeological Village in Al Dayer
59480428.s: Al Qaranah Archaeological Village is one of the heritage villages scattered across the mountains of Al Dayer Bani Malik governorate. It preserves the features of the old stone construction that characterises the villages of the area and, together with the surrounding villages and forts, forms part of the governorate's historical heritage.
59480428.b:
Al Qaranah Archaeological Village is one of the heritage villages scattered across the mountains of Al Dayer Bani Malik governorate. It preserves the features of the old stone construction that characterises the villages of the area and, together with the surrounding villages and forts, forms part of the governorate's historical heritage.

Al Dayer Bani Malik governorate lies east of the Jazan region in southern Saudi Arabia. It is known for towering heights, green terraces and archaeological castles scattered across the summits and heights that embrace the mist, in a scene of beauty that records the long past of these villages and buildings, with a wonderful architectural style and engineering art. In their features you can read longing and nostalgia for the past, now that modern civilisation has overtaken people, and you can sense the strength and skill of the design.

There is no valley or mountain that does not hold a number of villages and stone forts. For this reason Al Dayer Bani Malik governorate holds the largest concentration of stone forts in the world, which is evidence of the antiquity of human settlement and dense population, and of great progress in construction and agriculture in those eras.

One sign of the antiquity of the archaeological forts in Al Dayer and its mountains is the absence of mosques, congregational mosques and places of worship from their original designs, which means they predate the Islamic era. Some drawings and emblems belong to the first and second Himyarite periods. The forts also appear in ancient accounts, reaching back to the first millennium BC in some Thamudic, Lihyanite and Sabaean inscriptions. They appear after the birth of Christ in the Roman campaign against southern Arabia and in the accounts of the Himyarite king "Shammar Yuhar'ish". In the Islamic eras their accounts are many and scattered through the events of the Zaydi and Rasulid states and the states that arose in Tihama, down to modern history and the events of the Idrisid state and the flourishing Saudi era.

The archaeological castles and historic forts in Al Dayer take two forms, circular and square, which stand side by side in most castles and forts. Al Dayer governorate holds a rich historical heritage stretching back hundreds of years, in which a succession of civilisations with many historical events took shape. This is borne out by the large number of varied archaeological sites spread across many places and the inscriptions on them, and it is fertile ground for historical study.

59480424.s: Mathrarah Historic Village is one of the archaeological mountain villages in Al Dayer Bani Malik governorate and represents the traditional stone architecture for which the governorate's mountains are famous, with its houses built of stone on slopes overlooking the farming terraces.

59480405.s: Jazan Archaeological Museum is a museum in the city of Sabya in the Jazan region, next to the Idrisid archaeological site. It forms part of the network of museums established by the Antiquities and Museums Agency of the Ministry of Education. The museum was built in 1403 AH (1983 CE) and opened to visitors on 27 Muharram 1412 AH.
59480405.b:
Jazan Archaeological Museum is a museum in the city of Sabya in the Jazan region, next to the Idrisid archaeological site. It forms part of the network of museums established by the Antiquities and Museums Agency of the Ministry of Education. The museum was built in 1403 AH (1983 CE) and opened to visitors on 27 Muharram 1412 AH.

The museum has panels with maps showing the archaeological sites of the Jazan region, old photographs, Stone Age tools such as axes, scrapers and arrowheads, and examples of pottery, jewellery and ancient coins, as well as panels on ancient writings, scripts and languages. There are also panels and display cases on folk heritage, such as cooking utensils, clothing, jewellery and women's adornments, leatherwork and items made of palm fronds and leaves, and the crafts for which the Jazan region is known. The museum also tells the modern history of Jazan and its coming under Saudi rule at the hands of King Abdulaziz Al Saud. It has supporting sections including a laboratory and library and halls for seminars and lectures, and it was designed to be a centre for archaeological research and studies.
59480405.a: King Abdul Aziz Road, Al Nahdah, Sabya

59480245.s: Al Aridhah Viewpoint lies in Al Aridhah governorate and sits on a very high mountain, which makes it one of the most prominent viewpoints in the Jazan region.

59480087.t: Mohammed Harban Stadium (Rai') - The Stadium Carved into Al Hashr
59480087.s: In the Al Hashr mountains of Al Dayer Bani Malik governorate, east of the Jazan region, stands a unique sporting feat made by men who dug the earth and tamed the rock to build a football pitch. Mohammed Harban Al Harisi began this project in 2003 through personal effort, and the pitch carved into the rock has become a striking landmark of the Al Hashr mountains.

59480076.s: Wadi Al Futayhah is one of the valleys of the Jazan region in southern Saudi Arabia. It lies in Baish governorate, specifically north-east of Baish. The valley is known for water that flows all year round, fed by the overflow of the Wadi Baish Dam, which gives it permanent greenery and a large area of natural pasture that attracts many visitors.

59480072.t: The Black Mountain in Al Reeth
59480072.s: The Black Mountain, also called Jabal Al Azziyin after the Al Azziyin tribe, lies in Al Reeth governorate, east of the Jazan region in south-western Saudi Arabia.
59480072.b:
The Black Mountain, also called Jabal Al Azziyin after the Al Azziyin tribe, lies in Al Reeth governorate, east of the Jazan region in south-western Saudi Arabia.

The mountain is thought to be called the Black Mountain because of its dense vegetation, which gives it a black colour when seen from afar. It takes the form of an arc that begins in the north and curves toward the east at its highest peak. It is bordered to the north and north-west by Jabal Al Qahr and Wadi Lajab in Al Reeth governorate, and to the south by the Munjid mountains in Haroob governorate. The Sahalil mountains lie in the area south of the mountain.

The mountain is about 1,800 metres long and is home to more than two thousand people, most of whom work in farming and herding livestock. Like other people of the area's mountains, they are known for their traditional dress of shirt and waist wrap, along with fragrant plant leaves worn on their heads.

59480027.s: Wadi Lajab is a rift and fracture in the eastern part of Jabal Al Qahr (Zahwan), in Al Reeth governorate, which lies 150 kilometres north-east of the city of Jazan. It is considered one of the most important and prominent tourist sites and a place visited all year round by people from the region and other parts of the Kingdom. Like other tourist sites in the Jazan region, Wadi Lajab in Al Reeth governorate is seeing a growing number of visitors from inside and outside the region.
59480027.b:

Visitors can drive about 2 kilometres into the valley from the entrance, after which the valley passage narrows and continuing on foot becomes a pleasure, among the spray flying from the waterfalls and pools scattered along the valley and the golden sunlight that visits the valley for only a few hours, when it reaches the middle of the sky and its rays fall straight down. The place is made even more enjoyable and beautiful by the valley's hanging gardens on both sides, with dense palm trees at heights that may exceed 30 metres, among long-lived trees that cling to life, their roots stretching from about the middle of the valley's two edges down to the watercourse below.

59480009.s: The Hot Spring is in Al Aridhah governorate in the Jazan region. It is a group of natural springs that rise from underground at a high temperature of about 50 degrees Celsius, and visitors come for healing and relaxation. The spring lies within the Wadi Jazan Dam basin amid a forest of doum palms, which gives the place a natural beauty that combines therapeutic tourism and leisure.

59479561.s: The first mosque in the world built over the sea. It welcomes pilgrims and Umrah performers who come to visit it and is considered one of the most important landmarks in Jeddah; in 2009 the mosque received 20,000 visitors from among pilgrims and Umrah performers of many nationalities.
59479561.b:
The first mosque in the world built over the sea. It welcomes pilgrims and Umrah performers who come to visit it and is considered one of the most important landmarks in Jeddah; in 2009 the mosque received 20,000 visitors from among pilgrims and Umrah performers of many nationalities.

The mosque is a wonderful blend of modern and old architecture and Islamic art, built with the latest technology and equipment and with advanced sound and lighting systems. It has 52 external domes surrounding the mosque, in addition to the large main dome with eight bases in the middle, and 23 external canopies. It is embroidered inside and out with Quranic verses written in several different scripts such as naskh, ruq'ah and diwani.

The edges of the main dome hold stained glass that lets light, the rays of the sun, into the mosque through 56 windows around the dome, which is designed in the Islamic style. There are also arabesques and Islamic carvings on the walls and windows, and a wooden women's prayer gallery, suspended and raised in the last third of the mosque, which holds about 500 worshippers. The mosque also has service facilities, with areas set aside for ablution and toilets and comfortable, fully equipped prayer halls.

59460430.s: Al Birk Beach, also known as Al Mahaji Beach, lies north of Al Birk governorate in the Asir region and is known for its clean sandy soil. The beach is a favourite spot for diving lovers because of its coral reefs, and it also attracts anglers and those looking for a quiet coastal atmosphere away from the crowds.

59460405.s: Jabal Kudumbul Island is one of the islands in the Red Sea that belong to the Al Qahmah centre, part of the Asir region in south-western Saudi Arabia. Reaching the island takes 30 minutes by fishing boat. The island is known for its mountain, which takes up a large part of it and is visited by some anglers, and also for migratory falcons that pass over the mountain.

59460404.s: Wadi Dhahban Dam Lake is one of the natural bodies of water in the Asir region and a beautiful destination for nature lovers and lovers of striking water scenery. Behind the dam, rainwater collects amid green mountain terrain that surrounds it on all sides. The lake is a favourite destination for nature and photography enthusiasts, offering a calm atmosphere away from the bustle of the cities, and it becomes even more beautiful in the rainy seasons, when its water level rises.

It is rich in plants of all kinds, as well as old dams and wells.

59460395.t: Mohammed bin Adwan Al Ahmari Museum and Heritage Village
59460395.s: Mohammed bin Adwan Al Ahmari Museum is in the south of Saudi Arabia, specifically in Bal Ahmar. It was established in 2020 as one of the heritage projects in the area. The museum has 12 corners holding more than 3,000 historic archaeological items spread over four floors, conveying the history of the area's past inhabitants.
59460395.b:

The heritage village has hospitality majlis rooms, event halls and traditional restaurants serving visitors the area's most delicious heritage dishes. It also has a farm for wheat and another for strawberries, where visitors can stroll and pick the fruit, and a cafe known for the fresh strawberry juice made from the farm's produce.

59460394.t: Aqabat Al Ja'dah in Bal Ahmar
59460394.s: The Aqabat Al Ja'dah road, which leads down to Tihama and Asir and on to Muhayil governorate, shortens the journey by 170 km when descending to the Tihama region. Its crossing takes up to 15 minutes from the heights of the Hejaz mountains to the plains of Tihama, and it is also a good place for outings.

59440701.s: Dar Dahdooh Fort is one of the archaeological forts in Tanomah, part of the Asir region. It has three floors showing features of the area's heritage life: a floor devoted to handicrafts and leather goods, a floor for traditional weapons, and a floor for old jewellery and women's clothing. The fort gives visitors an introductory tour of the history of Tanomah and its authentic heritage through its varied collection, and its hosts take care to welcome visitors with dates, authentic butter and Arabic coffee in the traditional way, giving the experience a genuinely hospitable character.

59440657.t: Al Qarya Heritage Village in Tanomah
59440657.s: Al Qarya Heritage Village in Tanomah is an archaeological village with beautiful alleys and authentic construction. It has houses and small bridges built of stone, as well as a deep well and an old mosque. The village reflects the traditional mountain architecture of the Asir region and is a good destination for heritage and photography lovers who want to explore the details of old life.

The park is known for its talh, atm and juniper trees and some natural rock formations, making it a good destination for those who enjoy outings and watching mountain nature overlooking the coastal plains.
